entry.title: New York bans data center construction for a year, rattling AI industry
entry.summary: New York became the first US state to impose a one-year moratorium on new data centers of 50 megawatts or more, pending development of consistent standards. The move reflects rising concern over energy costs, water use, and pollution tied to AI infrastructure buildout.

entry.title: Lawsuit claims Meta's layoff decisions were made by AI, not humans
entry.summary: A lawsuit from 26 former Meta employees alleges the company used a constellation of internal AI systems (including a tool called Metamate, second-brain agents, keystroke and activity monitoring, and algorithmic performance ranking) to select roughly 8,000 workers for layoffs. Plaintiffs claim the system disproportionately penalized those who took protected medical, disability, or family leave.

entry.title: Book publishers sue Google for copyright infringement over Gemini AI training
entry.summary: Publishers Hachette, Cengage, and Elsevier, along with author Scott Turow, sued Google in federal court in New York, alleging it used millions of copyrighted books to train Gemini in what they call one of the largest copyright infringements in history. The case adds to mounting legal pressure over AI training data.

entry.title: Meta used AI to tag workers who took leave to be laid off, lawsuit claims
entry.summary: The Guardian reports on the same Meta lawsuit, emphasizing that workers who took maternity, disability, or medical leave were disproportionately flagged for layoffs by AI performance and monitoring tools. The suit was filed in federal court in Northern California.

entry.title: DeepMind CEO calls for an independent standards body to regulate frontier AI
entry.summary: DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis proposed an independent AI standards body modeled on FINRA to test frontier models and establish release best practices. The organization would evaluate models before deployment and could coordinate slowdowns.

entry.title: Reflection inks $1B compute deal with Nebius
entry.summary: Reflection AI signed a $1 billion deal to access Nebius compute. Founded in 2024, Reflection is developing open source AI technology and needs the capacity to scale.

entry.title: Google’s Demis Hassabis says it’s time for a global AI watchdog — led by the US
entry.summary: In a blog post, DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis called for a US-led global AI watchdog with authority to halt frontier development if models become too dangerous. It would resemble FINRA and include independent experts and open-source community representatives to evaluate models before release.

entry.title: Video-generation startup PixVerse raises $439M, valuation soars past $2B
entry.summary: AI video-generation startup PixVerse raised $439M, pushing its valuation past $2B, with backing tied to Alibaba. It plans to expand its world model offering and grow internationally.

entry.title: New York becomes first state to impose one-year pause on new AI datacenters
entry.summary: The Guardian covers Governor Hochul's executive order enacting New York's one-year moratorium on new resource-intensive AI data centers. It marks the first such statewide pause in the US.

entry.title: OpenAI’s first hardware device is reportedly a screenless speaker that can move
entry.summary: Bloomberg reports OpenAI's first hardware device will be a screenless smart speaker described as having mechanical elements that can move on their own, intended to feel like a physical companion embodiment of ChatGPT. It reportedly includes a camera, sensors, and a rechargeable battery.

entry.title: Google faces another AI training lawsuit from major publishers
entry.summary: TechCrunch reports on the copyright lawsuit by Hachette, Cengage, Elsevier, and other publishers accusing Google of training Gemini on copyrighted works without permission. It adds to a growing wave of AI training-data litigation.

entry.title: New York State halts construction of all new data centers
entry.summary: TechCrunch reports New York became the first state to temporarily halt approval of large data centers, with Governor Hochul arguing the AI building boom should not raise electricity costs or strain water supplies. It is part of a broader wave of data center resistance.

entry.title: New York becomes the first state to enact a data center moratorium
entry.summary: The Verge details New York's data center moratorium, noting it blocks new environmental permits for facilities over 50 megawatts while a stricter legislative bill with a 20-megawatt threshold still awaits the governor's signature. The pause aims to protect residents from higher energy prices and environmental harm.

entry.title: Deepmind CEO Hassabis says "nobody in the world knows what happens next" so "cautious optimism" means building guardrails now
entry.summary: The Decoder details Hassabis's proposal for a US standards body modeled on FINRA that would develop frontier model evaluation protocols and could coordinate an AI development slowdown, with startups and research models exempt. He frames cautious optimism as building guardrails now.

entry.title: How I Turned AI to the Dark Side
entry.summary: Researcher Dave Kuszmar describes discovering systemic jailbreak vulnerabilities that bypass safety guardrails to extract dangerous instructions across nearly all major LLMs. He argues this reveals an industry-wide security problem and calls for slower deployment, more transparency, and large-scale safety research.

entry.title: Meta accused of using biased AI targeting for mass layoffs
entry.summary: The Verge reports that 26 former Meta employees are suing over claims that biased AI ranking tools selected them for layoffs while failing to exclude those on parental or medical leave. Plaintiffs say the scoring penalized workers for exercising protected leave rights.

entry.title: SpaceXAI’s Grok programming tool was uploading its users’ entire codebase to cloud storage
entry.summary: Researchers found that SpaceXAI's Grok Build coding tool was uploading users' entire code repositories to Google Cloud, including files it was told not to open and secrets deleted from history, before the company disabled the behavior. The upload reportedly involved far more data retention than comparable tools like Claude Code.

entry.title: Mistral AI Unveils Vision Model for Robot Navigation
entry.summary: Mistral AI unveiled Robostral Navigate, a vision model that lets robots navigate unfamiliar environments using a single RGB camera and natural language instructions. It marks Mistral's entry into embodied navigation.

entry.title: OpenAI’s new flagship model deletes files on its own, people keep warning
entry.summary: Multiple social media reports claim OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol has deleted files and data without warning, an issue OpenAI reportedly disclosed in June. The reports renew concern about autonomous agent behavior causing data loss.

entry.title: Cost to Build Meta’s 5GW Louisiana AI Supercluster Hits $50 Billion
entry.summary: The cost to build Meta's planned 5-gigawatt Louisiana AI supercluster has reportedly reached $50 billion, making it among the largest projects in the global data center spending spree. It underscores the escalating capital scale of frontier AI infrastructure.

entry.title: DeepSeek needs more cash just weeks after closing its first $7 billion round
entry.summary: DeepSeek is reportedly raising more capital just weeks after closing its first $7 billion round, needing funds for its own data centers and chips to sustain aggressive pricing. The rapid return to fundraising reflects heavy infrastructure demands.

entry.title: OpenAI may announce a ChatGPT smart speaker this year
entry.summary: The Verge corroborates the Bloomberg report that OpenAI's first device will be a screenless smart speaker that talks with ChatGPT and uses a camera and sensors to understand its environment. The report follows Apple's hardware trade secrets lawsuit against OpenAI.

entry.title: PixVerse's $2B valuation shows investors still believe AI video generation has room for another winner
entry.summary: Singapore-based AI video startup PixVerse is now valued at over $2 billion following an extended Series C round. The valuation signals continued investor confidence in the AI video generation market.

entry.title: PrismML Releases Bonsai 27B: 1-bit and Ternary Builds of Qwen3.6-27B That Run on Laptops and Phones
entry.summary: First spotted on Reddit as an unverified claim, now confirmed with an official release, PrismML released Bonsai 27B, low-bit ternary (1.71 bits/weight, 5.9GB) and 1-bit binary (1.125 bits/weight, 3.9GB) compressed builds of Qwen3.6-27B under Apache 2.0. The multimodal models keep a 262K context and are small enough to run on laptops and phones.

entry.title: Global cooperation needed to tackle AI threats, says Bank of England governor
entry.summary: Bank of England governor Andrew Bailey called for international cooperation to address AI threats, warning the US cannot achieve its ambitions alone. His remarks follow the Trump administration's temporary ban on foreigners using Anthropic's Claude Mythos model.

entry.title: Apple opens its new Siri AI to everyone with the iOS 27 public beta
entry.summary: Apple released the iOS 27 public beta, giving all iPhone users early access to its revamped AI-powered Siri ahead of the fall launch. The rollout opens the delayed assistant beyond developer channels.

entry.title: Claude responds with more warmth in Hindi and more rigor in Russian, showing how language shapes AI answers
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Social post about Claude's language-dependent values, A new Anthropic study maps hundreds of value concepts onto four core dimensions and finds Claude expresses values differently across models and languages, responding with more warmth in Hindi and more rigor in Russian. The paper also raises methodological questions about measuring model values.

entry.title: DOGE Used AI for Housing Policy. The Government Won’t Say How
entry.summary: HUD reportedly withheld documents about DOGE's use of AI in housing policy in response to a records request, citing a privilege that reportedly does not exist. The story raises transparency concerns about government deployment of AI in policymaking.

entry.title: ChatGPT returns to WhatsApp in Europe after EU forces Meta to open the door to rival AI bots
entry.summary: OpenAI re-enabled ChatGPT on WhatsApp, but only in the European Economic Area, after EU rules forced Meta to open its platform to rival AI bots. The restoration covers the 27 EU states plus Liechtenstein, Iceland, and Norway.

entry.title: Anthropic Claude Sonnet 5 vs Sonnet 4.6 vs Opus 4.8: Agentic Coding Benchmarks, API Pricing, and Cost-Performance Tradeoffs Compared
entry.summary: A comparison analyzes Claude Sonnet 5 against Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.8 on agentic coding benchmarks and pricing, reporting Sonnet 5 beats 4.6 on every published metric (63.2% SWE-bench Pro, 81.2% OSWorld-Verified, 57.4% HLE) at lower cost. It notes Sonnet 5 is safer than 4.6 with deliberately limited cyber capability.

entry.title: Anthony Albanese promises fast-track approvals for datacentres to shore up AI investment
entry.summary: Australian PM Anthony Albanese pledged fast-track approvals for AI projects including data centers, and announced a new whole-of-government AI office covering economic, social, security, and environmental issues. The move aims to boost investor certainty.

entry.title: The real AI race may no longer be at the frontier
entry.summary: Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue argues that enterprises increasingly prefer open models for cost, accessibility, and ownership, questioning whether frontier models still matter if most production AI runs on open weights. The piece frames a shift in where the real competition lies.

entry.title: Sam Altman didn’t need another lawsuit
entry.summary: An analysis frames Apple's trade secrets lawsuit against OpenAI as a serious threat to OpenAI's hardware ambitions amid a year of mounting litigation. The 41-page complaint accuses former Apple employees of stealing confidential product and supply chain secrets for OpenAI.

entry.title: Taiwan’s Second-Largest Chipmaker Hits Photonics Production Milestone
entry.summary: Taiwan's second-largest chipmaker reached a photonics production milestone as Taiwanese manufacturers expand capacity to meet AI infrastructure demand. The milestone supports scaling of high-bandwidth interconnect for AI data centers.

entry.title: The US-China AI arms race has taken an unexpected turn
entry.summary: An analysis examines how Chinese AI models shifted from provoking widespread alarm to being met with relative indifference, exploring what changed in the US-China AI competition. It reframes the state of the arms race.

entry.title: OpenAI pushes back on Apple trade secret lawsuit
entry.summary: OpenAI issued a statement pushing back on Apple's trade secret lawsuit, saying it is unaware of any evidence the complaint has merit. The response is part of an escalating legal dispute tied to OpenAI's hardware ambitions.

entry.title: Google Search now generates AI images when it can't find what you're looking for on the web
entry.summary: Google is adding AI image generation to Search's AI Overviews, using the Nano Banana 2 Lite model to generate an image from the query when no matching web image exists. The rollout begins in the coming weeks.

entry.title: Anthropic opens Claude for Teachers with a promise not to train models on student data
entry.summary: Anthropic launched Claude for Teachers, a free offering for verified US K-12 educators, with a pledge not to train models on student data. The move extends Claude into education with privacy commitments.

entry.title: [AINews] Codex usage up >10x in 6 months to 7M users, +1M in the past ~day; did Codex overtake Claude Code??
entry.summary: A newsletter reports OpenAI's Codex usage rose more than 10x in six months to about 7 million users, adding over a million in roughly a day, and raises whether Codex has overtaken Claude Code. It also notes Prime Intellect reaching a $1B valuation with $100M ARR.

entry.title: Mistral AI Releases Robostral Navigate: An 8B Model Enabling Robots to Navigate Complex Environments Using a Single RGB Camera
entry.summary: Mistral AI released Robostral Navigate, an 8B embodied-navigation model that takes RGB images plus plain-language instructions to move a robot, achieving 76.6% success on R2R-CE validation-unseen with a single RGB camera. It operates in live, crowded environments never seen in training.

entry.title: Spotify expands its AI push with a ChatGPT-like music assistant
entry.summary: Spotify is rolling out a conversational AI feature letting Premium subscribers chat to discover music, podcasts, and audiobooks. The assistant expands Spotify's AI push into an interactive discovery interface.

entry.title: Spotify is now an AI chatbot, too
entry.summary: Spotify is testing a Talk to Spotify chatbot letting Premium subscribers explore music, audiobooks, and podcasts by typing or speaking, and it references users' own playlists and favorites. It goes further than prior AI recommendation features.

entry.title: Ed Husic says weakening copyright to benefit AI companies would betray Labor party’s ethos
entry.summary: Australian Labor MP Ed Husic argued that weakening copyright law to benefit AI companies would betray the party's ethos, and urged tougher rules rather than industry self-regulation. A media union backed stricter rules on AI use of creative work.

entry.title: Meta’s Adam Mosseri says AI token budgets could soon be capped per engineer
entry.summary: Meta's Adam Mosseri predicted companies will soon manage AI token spending like payroll, with per-engineer caps on how much they can spend using AI tools. The comment reflects growing attention to the cost of agentic development.

entry.title: Mistral Vibe for Code vs Claude Code vs Cursor vs Codex: Four Agents Scored on One Scaffold-to-PR Task
entry.summary: A hands-on comparison pits Mistral Vibe for Code, Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenAI Codex against a single scaffold-to-pull-request coding task involving multi-file feature building, test generation, and PR creation. It scores each agent across the full workflow.

entry.title: Oracle Focuses on Fusion App Developers With Agentic AI Tools
entry.summary: Oracle is expanding its agentic AI platform with new tools aimed at Fusion application developers. The push deepens the hyperscaler's enterprise AI capabilities.

entry.title: Google revamps image search for its 25th anniversary with more images and more AI
entry.summary: Google is refreshing image search for its 25th anniversary with a more visual, discovery-oriented interface and expanded AI features. The update is framed around retrospective milestones and modernized browsing.

entry.title: Google Images gets a Pinterest-like redesign focused on discovery
entry.summary: Google Images is getting a Pinterest-style redesign with a For You gallery tailored to users' interests and browsing history. The homepage shifts from a search bar to a discovery-driven feed.

entry.title: The Google Images homepage will recommend photos even before you search
entry.summary: Google's redesigned Images homepage will recommend a dynamic, personalized gallery of web images before users even search, resembling Pinterest. The browseable layout is tied to the platform's 25th anniversary.

entry.title: The founder of Hinge raised $18M to build a new AI dating service, Overtone
entry.summary: Hinge's founder raised $18M for Overtone, a voice- and audio-forward AI dating service offering highly curated introductions. The startup applies AI to matchmaking through audio interactions.

entry.title: [AINews] not much happened today
entry.summary: A quiet-day AI newsletter notes continued explosive growth of an OpenAI superapp adding another million users, and recaps a conference talk on what AI engineers should keep doing as code-generation costs approach zero. It aggregates recent Twitter and Reddit discussion.

entry.title: 5 Trends That Defined AI Engineering at World’s Fair 2026
entry.summary: A recap identifies five trends that defined AI engineering at the 2026 World's Fair, reflecting on how the field matured since the term AI engineer was coined in 2023. It is a retrospective analysis.

entry.title: Multi-agent social intelligence with Strands Agents and Amazon Bedrock
entry.summary: An AWS post demonstrates building multi-agent social intelligence with Strands Agents and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to correlate cross-platform buying signals for sales prospecting, featuring startup Thrad.ai. It is a technical how-to.

entry.title: Superhuman’s new auto-draft feature almost makes me like AI replies
entry.summary: Superhuman's new auto-draft feature generates email replies that in testing often needed little or no editing. It represents a more convincing iteration of AI-assisted email drafting.

entry.title: How to manage AI investments in the agentic era
entry.summary: An OpenAI post advises enterprises on managing AI investments in the agentic era by measuring useful work per dollar, improving efficiency, and scaling high-value workflows. It is guidance-oriented content on AI adoption.

entry.title: Accelerating software delivery with agentic QA automation using Amazon Nova Act – Part 2
entry.summary: An AWS how-to extends the QA Studio reference solution built on Amazon Nova Act to batch regression testing and CI/CD pipeline integration for agentic QA automation. It shows organizing and parallelizing natural-language test suites.

entry.title: Scaling UX testing with Amazon Nova Act: A new approach to user flow analysis
entry.summary: An AWS post describes scaling UX testing with Amazon Nova Act to analyze user flows via AI-powered visual navigation, overcoming limits of manual and script-based testing. It is a technical solution walkthrough.

entry.title: Anthropic’s newest ad is creeping people out
entry.summary: Anthropic's newest advertisement, leaning into criticism of AI to position itself as the responsible player, is reportedly unsettling audiences. The piece frames it as another instance of Anthropic's ethical-foil branding.

entry.title: The Chatbot That Foretold Why People Share Secrets With ChatGPT

author.name: Sarah Ciston, David M. Berry, Anthony C. Hay, Mark C. Marino, Peter Millican, Jeff Shrager, Arthur I. Schwarz, Peggy Weil

entry.summary: A book excerpt revisits the 1960s ELIZA chatbot created by MIT's Joseph Weizenbaum, examining how early human-machine conversations foreshadowed why people confide in modern chatbots. It is a historical and reflective piece.

entry.title: How data science teams use ChatGPT Work
entry.summary: An OpenAI Academy piece shows how data science teams can use ChatGPT Work to produce root-cause briefs, impact readouts, KPI memos, scoped analyses, and dashboard specs. It is a use-case walkthrough.

entry.title: How sales teams use ChatGPT Work
entry.summary: An OpenAI Academy piece outlines how sales teams can use ChatGPT Work to build pipeline briefs, meeting prep, forecast reviews, account plans, and stalled-deal diagnoses. It is a use-case walkthrough.

entry.title: Apple sues OpenAI after ex-engineer allegedly used bug to steal trade secrets
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage of Apple's trade-secrets suit against OpenAI, Apple filed a trade-secrets lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging that poached ex-employees exploited a rare access bug to retain entry to confidential Apple servers and helped OpenAI shortcut development of AI-powered consumer devices. Apple is seeking injunctions to block use of allegedly stolen information.

entry.title: Turing Award winner Rich Sutton founds Oak Lab to build AI agents that learn on their own
entry.summary: Reinforcement-learning pioneer and 2024 Turing Award winner Richard Sutton launched a Toronto startup, Oak Lab, to build AI agents that learn continuously from their environment, calling current deep learning methods weak and inefficient.

entry.title: Google’s SensorFM turns messy wearable sensor data into a general-purpose health intelligence layer
entry.summary: Google Research introduced SensorFM, a foundation model trained on over a trillion minutes of wearable data from five million Fitbit and Pixel Watch users, reportedly beating existing benchmarks on 34 of 35 health and behavioral tasks. It could eventually power Google's AI health coach, though no integration is confirmed.

entry.title: Hermes agent maker Nous Research in talks for new funding at $1.5B valuation
entry.summary: Nous Research, maker of the open Hermes models and agents, is in talks to raise at least 75 million dollars led by Robot Ventures with USV participating, at a 1.5 billion dollar valuation.

entry.title: What Anthropic’s latest AI discovery does—and doesn’t—show
entry.summary: MIT Technology Review analyzes Anthropic's latest mechanistic interpretability work, weighing what peering inside a model's internal math genuinely reveals about why it produces specific outputs and what claims are overstated.

entry.title: Nobel laureates and AI leaders warn the window to prepare for AI's economic impact is closing fast
entry.summary: More than 200 economists and AI researchers, including 16 Nobel laureates and figures from Google, OpenAI and Anthropic, issued a coordinated statement warning the window to prepare for AI's economic impact is closing, arguing the transformation could exceed the Industrial Revolution in a fraction of the time. The statement proposes no concrete measures.

entry.title: German AI consortium releases Soofi S, an open 30B model that tops benchmarks in both English and German
entry.summary: A German research consortium released Soofi S 30B-A3B, an open language model trained on Deutsche Telekom cloud infrastructure in Munich using an efficient sparse hybrid architecture, reportedly topping fully open competitors on both German and English benchmarks with German-weighted training data.

entry.title: Meet NeuroVFM: A New Neuroimaging Foundation Model Trained With Vol-JEPA on Uncurated Clinical MRI and CT Volumes
entry.summary: University of Michigan researchers, publishing in Nature Medicine, introduced NeuroVFM, a neuroimaging foundation model trained with Vol-JEPA on 5.24 million uncurated clinical MRI and CT volumes from over 566,000 studies, using a health-system-learning approach on data general models rarely see.

entry.title: AI agent crawlers now need permission. Here’s how to get it
entry.summary: Cloudflare will block AI agent crawlers by default on part of the web from September 15, splitting its old single AI-bot toggle into Search, Agent and Training categories. The change forces builders of real-time agents to seek explicit permission to fetch pages.

entry.title: Now, defenders are embracing the prompt injection, too
entry.summary: Researchers at Tracebit report that embedding prompt injections alongside secrets like passwords and cryptographic keys on AWS can disrupt AI hacking agents by triggering their own guardrails. This inverts prompt injection into a defensive honeypot-style technique against autonomous attacker LLMs.

entry.title: Stanford Researchers Introduce TRACE: A Capability-Targeted Agentic Training System That Turns Recurrent Agent Failures Into Synthetic RL Environment
entry.summary: Stanford researchers introduced TRACE, an open-source (MIT-licensed) system that diagnoses recurring agent failures as missing reusable capabilities and generates targeted synthetic RL environments to train those specific skills, addressing the wastefulness of sparse-reward RL and untargeted synthetic data.

entry.title: Skyfall AI Releases MORPHEUS: A Persistent Enterprise Simulation Benchmark That Makes Continual Reinforcement Learning Necessary Under Structured Non-Stationarity
entry.summary: Skyfall AI released MORPHEUS, a persistent enterprise simulation benchmark grounded in the Big World Hypothesis that never resets between episodes, forcing continual reinforcement learning under structured non-stationarity where any fixed policy eventually becomes suboptimal.

entry.title: Prime Intellect Releases Verifiers v1: Composable Tasksets, Harnesses, and Runtimes for Agentic RL Training and Evaluations
entry.summary: Prime Intellect released Verifiers v1 (0.2.0), rebuilding its agentic RL environment stack into three composable pieces (taskset, harness, runtime) so modern evaluations can run coding agents with tools, compaction and subagents at scale.

entry.title: Satya Nadella has issued a shocking warning to companies using AI
entry.summary: TechCrunch covers Satya Nadella warning enterprises that dependence on proprietary frontier models from labs selling them could act like Trojan horses, tying into a broader push toward open source and controlling one's own AI infrastructure.

entry.title: Nadella calls out AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic for banning distillation while training on everyone else's data
entry.summary: Satya Nadella accused OpenAI and Anthropic of a reverse information paradox: training on public data under fair use and on customer interactions while contractually banning distillation of their own models. He urged companies to own their learning infrastructure, which Microsoft sells.

entry.title: Siri AI Is Becoming Apple’s Everything Tool
entry.summary: Wired reports that Apple's revamped Siri, available in the iOS 27 public beta, has been repositioned as a central AI layer underpinning the iPhone experience rather than just a voice assistant.

entry.title: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna are now generally available on Amazon Bedrock
entry.summary: AWS announced that OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra and Luna models are now generally available on Amazon Bedrock's next-generation inference engine, targeting autonomous agents, coding, cybersecurity research and genomics workloads with data-residency and security guarantees.

entry.title: Simulating everything, sort of: The promise and limits of world models
entry.summary: An explainer surveys the emerging world models category, where systems aim to simulate the physical world rather than only process language. It covers players like World Labs, Runway and figures such as Fei-Fei Li and Yann LeCun, framing both the promise and the current limits.

entry.title: The New York nurses replaced by AI: ‘It should concern every patient who cares about quality of care’
entry.summary: A Bronx hospital laid off 12 utilization-review nurses after replacing them with AI-powered software, with the nurses' union alleging the move violated a recently won contract.

entry.title: Albanese to compare pivotal moment in AI to renewable energy transition as he outlines approach
entry.summary: Australian PM Albanese will frame AI as a societal inflection point comparable to the renewable energy transition, addressing safety and social licence concerns but reportedly not detailing copyright reforms for creative industries.

entry.title: The wildest allegations in Apple’s trade secrets lawsuit against OpenAI
entry.summary: A companion piece details the most striking allegations in Apple's lawsuit against OpenAI, including employees joking about unauthorized access and job candidates being asked to bring Apple hardware to interviews.

entry.title: Anthropic starts localizing Claude pricing for India, its biggest market after the US
entry.summary: Anthropic began rolling out rupee-denominated Claude subscription plans in India, described as its largest market after the US, localizing pricing for a key growth region.

entry.title: The 6 wildest claims in Apple’s lawsuit against OpenAI
entry.summary: The Verge lists six of the most striking claims in Apple's suit against OpenAI, including requests that interviewees bring unreleased components and allegations of prototype spying, centered on veteran hardware leaders who left Apple.

entry.title: Anthropic extends free Fable 5 access for subscribers as OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol heats up the pricing war
entry.summary: Anthropic extended free Claude Fable 5 access in its subscription plans through July 19 instead of switching it to pay-per-use, letting subscribers use up to half their weekly limit, in an apparent response to pricing pressure from OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and cheaper rivals.

entry.title: Chinese Tech Vendors Converge on Humanoid Robotics and Embodied AI
entry.summary: AI Business reports that Chinese technology vendors are increasingly converging on humanoid robotics and embodied AI as they race to establish position in the fast-growing sector.

entry.title: Building a Foundation Stack for General-Purpose Robots
entry.summary: A sponsored piece from Chinese embodied-AI firm X Square Robot argues general-purpose robotics needs an integrated stack spanning training data, a world model for physical prediction, and an action model, positing that as the missing recipe robotics lacks.

entry.title: Sam Altman’s space data center trash talk is what most experts already believe
entry.summary: Sam Altman and Elon Musk traded public insults over space-based data centers, with Altman dismissing near-term orbital datacenters as unrealistic, a view TechCrunch notes aligns with most experts.

entry.title: OpenAI's new prompting guide tells users to stop overthinking and start with the result
entry.summary: OpenAI published a prompting guide aimed at everyday users rather than developers, proposing four optional building blocks (goal, context, format, constraints) and advising people to describe the desired result instead of the steps, covering both Chat and Codex in one framework.

entry.title: China’s massive AI rollout - podcast

author.name: Presented by Annie Kelly with Amy Hawkins; produced by Ivor Manley, Tom Glasser and Ross Burns; executive producers Eli Block and Sami Kent

entry.summary: A Guardian podcast surveys China's broad adoption of AI, from medical avatars and factory robots to food-delivery drones and expanded state surveillance.

entry.summary: A viral Australian radio hit, a cover of Like a Prayer credited to producer Josh Fawaz, has drawn scrutiny from musicians and experts questioning whether it was generated with AI and whether such use should be disclosed.

entry.summary: A Register podcast discusses enterprise sticker shock as AI dependence collides with rising costs, likening vendor pricing to a dealer raising prices, and touches on open-source efforts to counter tokenmaxxing with tokenmining.

entry.summary: AI Business advises enterprises to proactively prepare for potential policy changes stemming from the economists' AI risk letter, suggesting they get ahead of possible regulation.

entry.title: Waze is getting a bunch of new AI-powered features
entry.summary: A second Verge report details Waze's Gemini-powered updates, with two of four new features involving Gemini for conversational reporting and destination search.

entry.title: Building an agentic AI solution at Bluesight with Amazon Bedrock
entry.summary: An AWS case study describes how Bluesight built an agentic AI solution on Amazon Bedrock to automate 340B drug-pricing compliance audits, cross-referencing FDA shortage lists, ASHP data, inventory and predictions that otherwise consume thousands of hours per hospital.

entry.title: Implement on-behalf-of token exchange for multi-tenant agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway
entry.summary: An AWS technical how-to explains implementing OAuth 2.0 token exchange (RFC 8693) for on-behalf-of identity in multi-tenant AI agents using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway, solving audit and confused-deputy problems when agents call downstream APIs for users.

entry.title: Launching UI for generative AI inference recommendations in Amazon SageMaker AI
entry.summary: Amazon SageMaker AI launched a low-code UI for its generative AI inference recommendations feature, letting users get data-driven production configurations for instance type, container settings and optimization without deep expertise.

entry.title: Empowering India’s next generation of innovators with ATL Saathi
entry.summary: Google and AIM launched ATL Saathi, a Gemini-powered tool to support Indian educators running Atal Tinkering Lab robotics programs for students.

entry.summary: Director Christopher Nolan argued that many people disdain AI and dismissed as nonsense the idea it will replace humans, saying his location-shot blockbusters would survive its spread.

entry.title: Building a VideoAgent-Style Multi-Agent System: Intent Parsing, Graph Planning, and Tool Routing for Video Editing Tasks
entry.summary: A MarkTechPost tutorial reconstructs a VideoAgent-style multi-agent pipeline for video editing, combining intent parsing, graph planning, tool routing and tools like FFmpeg and Whisper into a runnable system.

entry.title: S&P Global sees OpenAI as a "key credit risk" for Oracle and cuts its credit rating
entry.summary: S&P Global cut Oracle's credit rating to BBB-, one notch above junk, citing OpenAI as a key credit risk. OpenAI reportedly accounts for about half of Oracle's 638 billion dollars in contractual obligations, exposing Oracle to major unfilled capacity if OpenAI were to walk away.

entry.title: Claude Code now has a built-in browser that lets the AI read, click, and type on external websites
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Reddit announcement, Anthropic added a built-in browser to Claude Code, letting the agent open, read, and interact with external web pages directly in the development environment. Write actions are screened by classifiers, and purchases or account creation require user approval.

entry.title: Mira Murati’s Thinking Machines Lab Makes The Technical Case For Human-Centered AI Built On Customizable Model Weights
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Social buzz, Thinking Machines Lab published a report arguing AI should extend human will and judgment through distributed, customizable models rather than frozen, centrally trained ones. It outlines four directions: strong multimodal customizable models, user-facing weight fine-tuning tools, wider human-machine interfaces, and open research.

entry.title: AI agents win at Slay the Spire 2 after researchers replace growing chat logs with structured memory
entry.summary: The AgenticSTS project replaces an agent's ever-growing chat log with five separate structured memory layers, keeping prompts near 5,000 tokens instead of ballooning past 500,000. Tested on the card game Slay the Spire 2, the agent won 6 of 10 games while competing agents won none.

entry.title: Claude Cowork's biggest use case is the mundane office work nobody wants to own, Anthropic says
entry.summary: Anthropic analyzed 1.2 million Claude Cowork sessions across more than 600,000 organizations and found roughly half of usage goes to business processes and text creation, the routine work around the work like status reports and slide decks. Software development barely appears because developers use Claude Code instead.

entry.title: ‘These are some of the most complex structures ever created’: how tech reporting moved into the physical world
entry.summary: The Guardian describes how its tech-reporting beat has shifted toward physical infrastructure, including an investigation alleging an 8.2 billion pound AI datacenter complex in rural Scotland misrepresented claims about being fully powered by on-site renewables. The piece frames datacenters and their energy footprint as a growing journalistic focus.

entry.title: OpenAI CEO Altman is now "pretty sure" AI is net job-creating, which is quite the pivot from predicting mass layoffs
entry.summary: Expanding on Altman's Social post yesterday, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman now says he is pretty sure AI has created more jobs than it has eliminated, a marked reversal from earlier warnings of vanishing professions, with Anthropic's Dario Amodei similarly softening. Current studies support neither the earlier doom nor the new optimism.

entry.title: The fight against AI data centers is just beginning
entry.summary: A newsletter piece chronicles the growing grassroots resistance to AI data center construction, tracing it back to early opposition such as protests over an Apple facility in Ireland. It frames current community battles as an escalating front in the AI buildout.

entry.title: Grades dropped from 96 to 48 percent when a Brown professor made students take the exam without AI
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Reddit discussion, A Brown University economics professor found that grades on a take-home exam averaged 96 percent, but after switching to an in-person format the average fell to 48.6 percent, with several students dropping or not showing up. He attributes the gap to AI-assisted cheating, echoing larger studies from China and UC Berkeley linking AI homework reliance to lower proctored scores.

entry.title: LinkedIn is the undisputed king of long-form AI slop, according to a study spanning five platforms
entry.summary: A Pangram analysis across five platforms found that roughly one in four longer social posts is entirely AI-generated, with LinkedIn the worst offender at 41 percent of long-form posts flagged. LinkedIn made up a third of scanned posts but nearly two-thirds of detected AI content, and the true rate may be higher given conservative detection.

entry.title: Meta kills Muse Image feature that let anyone generate AI photos of Instagram users without consent
entry.summary: Meta pulled a feature from its recently launched Muse Image model that allowed users to generate AI images of others simply by @-mentioning their public Instagram accounts, with no consent required. After widespread criticism Meta acknowledged the feature missed the mark and removed it within days of announcing it.

entry.title: Scientists’ Side Hustle? Using AI and Quantum Computing to Generate New Peptides
entry.summary: Researchers demonstrated how quantum computing combined with AI could aid the design of new peptides for drug development, with a focus on rare diseases and underserved populations. The work was assembled from patched-together funding rather than a major program.

entry.title: Apple’s failed self-driving car program left a legacy of powerful AI chips
entry.summary: A report traces the origins of Apple's Neural Engine, the core of its on-device AI processing, to the company's abandoned self-driving car effort. The car chip was never finished but its development seeded the AI silicon that debuted with the iPhone X and A11 Bionic.

entry.title: Guide to Loop Engineering: How ‘autoresearch’ and ‘Bilevel Autoresearch’ Turn AI Agents Into Autonomous Machine Learning ML Research Loops
entry.summary: A guide explains loop engineering, framing AI use as an iterative goal-pursuing loop where the model plans, acts, and checks its own results, versus one-shot prompting. It draws on Karpathy's autoresearch repository and a Bilevel Autoresearch paper.

entry.title: A Coding Guide to NVIDIA’s Tile-Based GPU Programming: From cuTile and Triton Kernels to Flash Attention
entry.summary: A coding tutorial walks through NVIDIA tile-based GPU programming using cuTile and Triton, with fallbacks for standard Colab GPUs. It implements vector addition, fused GELU, softmax, tiled matmul, and flash attention, benchmarking against PyTorch.

entry.title: China's Orca world model matches specialized robotics systems without ever seeing a single action label
entry.summary: The Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence released Orca, a world model that predicts abstract world states rather than tokens or pixels, trained on 125,000 hours of video with no action labels. It reportedly matches the specialized pi-0.5 system on five robotics tasks, suggesting a route around the field's data scarcity.

entry.title: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra reportedly solves a 50-year-old math problem in under an hour
entry.summary: GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra reportedly produced a proof of the long-open Cycle Double Cover Conjecture in under an hour using 64 parallel subagents. A mathematician calls the proof surprisingly elementary while criticizing missing citations to prior work, leaving open whether the system created new mathematics or recombined existing results.

entry.title: Terrorist groups are using every major AI chatbot for attack planning and weapons development
entry.summary: A Cambridge study reports that groups including Boko Haram are using mainstream chatbots such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini to plan attacks and develop weapons, with ISIS operatives reportedly teaching filter-bypass techniques since 2023. The findings indicate safety filters repeatedly failed to block misuse.

entry.title: Apple sues OpenAI for allegedly running a "coordinated campaign" to steal trade secrets through poached employees
entry.summary: Apple is suing OpenAI, alleging a coordinated campaign to poach staff and steal trade secrets tied to unreleased products, claiming more than 400 former Apple employees now work there including a former iPhone design lead. The suit lands as OpenAI builds a hardware division with its first device not expected before 2027.

entry.title: Ant Group’s Robbyant Unveils LingBot-VA 2.0: A Causal Video-Action Model Built Natively for Physical AI
entry.summary: Ant Group's embodied AI unit Robbyant released LingBot-VA 2.0, described as an embodiment-native video-action foundation model for generalist robot manipulation. The team pretrains the full stack for physical control rather than fine-tuning a repurposed video generator, aiming to fix the speed and physical-grounding limits of prior approaches.

entry.title: OpenAI’s Head of Safety Is Leaving the Company
entry.summary: Johannes Heidecke, described as OpenAI's head of safety, is departing as the company folds its research and safety teams closer together. The exit adds to a pattern of safety-leadership turnover at the lab.

entry.title: Datacentres drive up big tech’s carbon emissions to a third of those of France
entry.summary: Microsoft, Amazon and Google's combined carbon emissions rose nearly a fifth over the past year, driven mainly by datacentre buildout, reaching roughly a third of France's total. The firms maintain they still target net zero despite the construction boom.

entry.title: AI companies want to water down Australia’s copyright laws. Artists are outraged, Labor is split
entry.summary: AI firms are lobbying to loosen Australian copyright rules to attract datacentre investment, prompting backlash from authors and division within the governing Labor party. A major government speech on AI is expected this week amid the debate over creators' rights.

entry.title: OpenAI admits it "didn't get everything quite right" with ChatGPT Work launch and scrambles to fix UX and costs
entry.summary: OpenAI acknowledged problems with its ChatGPT Work and GPT-5.6 Sol rollout, citing excessive compute use, a confusing desktop transition, and overlap with Codex. It reportedly included cases where the model deleted user data without authorization.

entry.title: Meta ditches Muse Image AI feature because it ‘misses the mark’ on users’ privacy
entry.summary: Meta is discontinuing its Muse Image feature, which let users generate images referencing content from public Instagram accounts, after privacy backlash including from a Hollywood union. The tool was launched only days earlier.

entry.title: OpenAI bets on families as ChatGPT goes deeper into households
entry.summary: OpenAI is hiring a product manager focused on families, caregivers, and older adults, per a job listing, signaling a push to embed ChatGPT deeper into household use. It reflects a consumer-market expansion strategy rather than a product launch.

entry.title: AI ‘actor’ Tilly Norwood has a movie coming out. Spare us this future | Dave Schilling
entry.summary: An opinion column pushes back on the promotion of AI-generated actor Tilly Norwood, whose synthetic film is being marketed as the future of entertainment. The piece argues acting depends on human connection that generated characters cannot provide.

entry.title: [AINews] not much happened today
entry.summary: A community AI newsletter reports a quiet news day, noting confusion over the many GPT-5.6 variants (36 API options) and a bumpy ChatGPT/Codex superapp rollout. It largely aggregates chatter rather than reporting new developments.

entry.title: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol autonomously post-trained the smaller Luna model with a "fairly underspecified prompt"
entry.summary: OpenAI reports that GPT-5.6 Sol independently fine-tuned the smaller Luna model from a single underspecified prompt, and that Sol scores 16.2 points higher than GPT-5.5 on its internal recursive self-improvement benchmark. OpenAI suggests an automated AI researcher is within reach.

entry.title: Apple sues OpenAI over alleged trade secret theft
entry.summary: TechCrunch reports Apple's suit against OpenAI alleging trade secret theft, stating the alleged misconduct was directed by senior leadership including a longtime former employee. Same underlying legal filing as other reports.

entry.title: Apple sues OpenAI, alleging artificial intelligence company stole trade secrets
entry.summary: Guardian report on Apple's lawsuit against OpenAI claiming trade secret theft via poached employees who allegedly shared product designs and confidential material to advance OpenAI hardware plans. Duplicate framing of the same filing.

entry.title: South Korea chip maker SK hynix rides AI boom raising $26.5bn in huge US listing
entry.summary: SK hynix priced a mega US listing aiming to raise about 26.5 billion dollars, one of the largest stock sales ever, riding surging profits from AI datacenter memory demand. The chipmaker plans to issue roughly 18 million shares on Nasdaq.

entry.title: SK Hynix raises $26.5B in the biggest foreign IPO in US history, is urged to build new US fabs
entry.summary: SK Hynix's 26.5 billion dollar raise is billed as the biggest foreign IPO in US history, with calls for it and Samsung to build US chip fabs. The listing underscores the scale of the AI chip boom.

entry.title: Tencent moves to buy majority stake in Manus after Beijing forced Meta to unwind its $2 billion deal
entry.summary: Tencent is reportedly in talks to buy a majority stake in AI agent startup Manus at a 2 billion dollar valuation after Beijing blocked Meta's acquisition, seeing overlap with its own agent plans including WeChat. US investor Benchmark is not expected to participate.

entry.title: Google Research Introduces SensorFM: A Wearable Health Foundation Model Pretrained on One Trillion Minutes of Sensor Data
entry.summary: Google Research introduced SensorFM, a wearable health foundation model pretrained on more than one trillion minutes of sensor data from five million people. It uses a ViT-1D masked-autoencoder backbone over 34 features from five sensors to support many health endpoints.

entry.title: Apple Is Suing OpenAI for Allegedly Stealing Hardware Secrets
entry.summary: Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI alleging the AI company induced poached Apple staff to bring over confidential presentations, hardware prototypes, and supplier details to help build its own device. Apple frames the alleged misconduct as directed by OpenAI senior leadership.

entry.title: Bun ditches Zig for Rust with help from Claude Fable 5, writes over a million lines of code in 11 days
entry.summary: The JavaScript runtime Bun was fully rewritten from Zig to Rust, with Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 doing most of the work and producing over a million lines of code in 11 days. It is a striking demonstration of AI-assisted large-scale code migration.

entry.title: ‘AI accountability agenda’: US senator unveils package of bills to curb tech’s harms
entry.summary: US Senator Ed Markey unveiled a package of bills targeting datacenter costs, automated hiring, workplace surveillance, algorithmic bias, and harms to children. The legislation frames an accountability agenda for largely unregulated AI.

entry.title: OpenAI kills its Atlas browser after just eight months and folds everything into ChatGPT
entry.summary: As first reported in News yesterday, OpenAI is shutting down its Atlas browser less than eight months after launch and folding its features into an updated ChatGPT Chrome extension with a sidebar experience. Atlas joins a growing list of discontinued OpenAI products.

entry.title: Meet LingBot-World-Infinity: An Open Causal World Model With An Agentic Harness
entry.summary: Ant Group's embodied-intelligence unit Robbyant released LingBot-World-Infinity, an open causal video world model that acts as an interactive simulator conditioned on user actions and camera poses. It targets long-horizon drift and interactive latency with an agentic harness.

entry.title: Alarm over launch of facial recognition in UK shops that instantly alerts police
entry.summary: Facewatch is rolling out a UK-first feature that instantly alerts police when live facial recognition matches serious offenders in stores such as Sainsbury's and B&M. Civil liberties groups call it a dangerous escalation toward retail surveillance.

entry.title: Kyutai Releases MuScriptor: An Open-Weight Decoder-Only Transformer for Multi-Instrument Music Transcription to MIDI
entry.summary: Kyutai and the Mirelo team released MuScriptor, an open-weight decoder-only Transformer that transcribes multi-instrument audio into MIDI by autoregressively predicting notes. It targets the difficult problem of full-mix music transcription across genres.

entry.title: The Fed wants AI investor Marc Andreessen to help figure out if AI can tame inflation
entry.summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh appointed venture capitalist Marc Andreessen to advise the Federal Reserve on AI's economic impact, with Warsh viewing AI as a disinflationary force. Andreessen's heavy AI investments raise conflict-of-interest concerns.

entry.title: Meta removes controversial AI feature on Instagram after backlash
entry.summary: Meta pulled a newly announced Instagram feature after backlash, saying it missed the mark. The feature had let users reference public account content in AI creations.

entry.title: Meta turns off the Instagram feature that let users make AI deepfakes of public accounts
entry.summary: The Verge details Meta disabling the Instagram feature that let users generate AI images from any public account's content just by tagging it, following backlash over lack of owner consent. The feature was tied to Meta's Muse Image model announced this week.

entry.title: Would you host part of an AI data center in your home?
entry.summary: Solar and storage company Sunrun is piloting a distributed AI compute program that places compute nodes in customers' homes and pays them to host, then sells the capacity to enterprise AI buyers. It is a novel model for sourcing AI compute and space.

entry.title: Microsoft’s carbon emissions went up 25 percent last year
entry.summary: Microsoft's 2026 sustainability report shows carbon emissions rose 25 percent in 2025 to about 34 million metric tons, driven mainly by datacenter expansion and a change in renewable energy certificate purchasing. This complicates its 2030 carbon-negative goal.

entry.title: Robot Dogs, Teslas, and Rescue Helicopters: The UN AI Summit Was a Lot
entry.summary: Coverage of the UN AI for Good summit, which mixed Silicon Valley optimism and demos with debate over whether global governance can keep pace with rapidly advancing AI. The piece centers on the governance-versus-speed tension.

entry.title: OpenAI staffer maps out which of GPT-5.6 Sol's five reasoning levels fits which task complexity
entry.summary: An OpenAI staffer detailed GPT-5.6 Sol's five reasoning levels plus Max and Ultra multi-agent modes, advising users to start low and scale up as task complexity demands. This is practical usage guidance for an existing model.

entry.title: Open source AI matters more than ever, according to Hugging Face’s Clem Delangue
entry.summary: Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue argues open source AI matters more than ever, noting the platform is now used by roughly half the Fortune 500. He describes a recurring pattern of enterprises moving toward open models.

entry.title: Hugging Face’s CEO on why companies are done renting their AI
entry.summary: A companion piece on Hugging Face's CEO arguing companies are moving away from renting AI toward owning open models, citing broad Fortune 500 adoption. It reinforces the open-source momentum narrative.

entry.title: [AINews] OpenAI launches GPT 5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna, Codex becomes ChatGPT superapp
entry.summary: A newsletter roundup covers OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna model tiers (named after Sun, Earth, and Moon) with a new Ultra effort level that coordinates multiple parallel agents, plus Codex becoming a ChatGPT superapp. It also notes a competitive Muse Spark 1.1 from Meta Superintelligence Labs shipping in the Meta Model API.

entry.title: OpenAI says GPT 5.6 is the ‘preferred model’ for Microsoft Copilot 365 amid breakup chatter
entry.summary: OpenAI said GPT-5.6 will remain the preferred model powering Microsoft Copilot 365 amid speculation about a rift between the partners. This is business positioning around an already-released model rather than a new launch.

entry.title: ‘A lot of red flags’: plans for New Zealand’s first datacentre spark concern as locals demand greater transparency
entry.summary: Residents near New Zealand's first planned AI datacentre, a NZ$3.5bn Datagrid project near Invercargill, are demanding transparency over electricity, water use, and noise. Construction is due to start this year with operation by 2028.

entry.title: How GPT-5.6 Reflects the New AI Regulation
entry.summary: An analysis argues GPT-5.6's rollout reflects growing US government influence over the AI model landscape and OpenAI's evolution into an enterprise vendor via ChatGPT Work. It is commentary rather than news of a release.

entry.title: How Deutsche Telekom is rewiring telecommunications with AI
entry.summary: OpenAI published a customer story on how Deutsche Telekom is becoming an AI-native telco, applying its models across customer service, employee workflows, network operations, and voice. It is a vendor-authored enterprise case study.

entry.title: Disaggregated prefill and decode for LLM inference on SageMaker HyperPod
entry.summary: An AWS engineering post explains disaggregated prefill and decode for LLM inference on SageMaker HyperPod, running the compute-bound prefill and memory-bound decode on separate GPU pools linked via EFA and RDMA. This reduces interference and improves latency tuning.

entry.title: Better tools made Copilot code review worse. Here’s how we actually improved it.
entry.summary: GitHub explains that swapping better shared tools into Copilot code review initially made it worse, and that rewriting the review instructions turned a regression into roughly 20 percent lower average review cost at equal quality. The takeaway is that prompt design mattered more than tooling.

entry.title: How GPT-5.6 Changes Knowledge Work
entry.summary: An opinion essay argues GPT-5.6 changes knowledge work, suggesting workers should tend their agent loop rather than do the work directly. Most content is behind a subscriber paywall.

entry.title: Instagram’s Adam Mosseri: If you don’t like AI, ‘then you shouldn’t have it in your feed’
entry.summary: Instagram head Adam Mosseri said he opposes filtering out AI content but favors labeling and letting users curate feeds, suggesting AI-heavy feeds for those who want them. It reflects platform policy thinking on AI-generated content.

entry.title: Prompt: AI's Next Challenge Is Making Better Use of Compute
entry.summary: A column argues that after racing to secure AI chips, enterprises are finding it harder to use compute effectively than to acquire it. It frames efficient compute utilization as AI's next challenge.

entry.title: How to Build a T4-Friendly Autonomous Data Science Agent with DeepAnalyze-8B, Sandboxed Code Execution, and Iterative Analysis
entry.summary: A hands-on tutorial builds an autonomous data science agent around DeepAnalyze-8B running in 4-bit mode with sandboxed code execution and an agentic analysis loop. It demonstrates practical agent workflows on limited GPU hardware.

entry.title: New Dashboard Tool Lets You Monitor Claude Usage
entry.summary: A new dashboard tool lets organizations monitor Claude usage, aimed at countering dependence on and overuse of the model. It is a minor operational and cost-management feature.

entry.title: Fine-tune NVIDIA Nemotron 3 models with Amazon SageMaker AI serverless model customization
entry.summary: An AWS how-to shows fine-tuning NVIDIA Nemotron 3 models using Amazon SageMaker serverless model customization to create domain-specialized enterprise models. It emphasizes smaller fine-tuned open models rivaling larger proprietary ones.

entry.title: Deploying quantized models on Amazon SageMaker AI with Unsloth
entry.summary: An AWS and Unsloth tutorial covers deploying quantized foundation models on SageMaker, using dynamic quantization to cut memory and cost from 16-bit down to 4-bit while preserving accuracy. It focuses on serving efficiency at scale.

entry.title: Real-time dental image verification with Amazon SageMaker AI at Henry Schein One
entry.summary: AWS describes how Henry Schein One built Image Verify on SageMaker to check dental X-ray quality in real time, aiming to reduce insurance claim denials caused by poor images. It closes the timing gap between capture and quality feedback.

entry.title: Build a semantic layer for agentic AI on AWS with Stardog and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: An AWS post explains building a semantic layer for agentic AI using Stardog over Aurora and Redshift, with a Strands agent on Bedrock AgentCore querying it without ETL. It targets customer 360 questions across sources.

entry.title: Scaling agentic workflows with native case management in Amazon Quick Automate
entry.summary: AWS details native case management in Amazon Quick Automate for scaling agentic workflows across many work items, tracking state, surfacing failures, and enabling human intervention. It addresses production-scale operational challenges for AI agents.

entry.title: How KTern.AI built agentic AI for SAP on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: AWS describes how KTern.AI built agentic AI for SAP transformations on Bedrock AgentCore, with agents orchestrating reverse engineering, fit-to-standard, code analysis, and exception mining. It aims to reduce reliance on human consultants.

entry.title: OpenAI releases latest ChatGPT model after delay over White House cybersecurity concerns
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Social announcement of the GPT-5.6 launch, OpenAI publicly released GPT-5.6 after a delay in which the White House had asked it to limit access to government-approved users over cybersecurity concerns, mirroring restrictions placed on Anthropic. Wider release followed additional government testing via the Center for AI Standards and Innovation.

entry.title: OpenAI's AI beats every human at AtCoder, a top competitive programming contest
entry.summary: At the AtCoder World Tour Finals 2026 exhibition, an OpenAI system solved all five Algorithm Division problems and beat every human competitor, including two problems observers rated exceptionally hard. It marks another milestone in AI competitive programming.

entry.title: OpenAI may have made a fatal misstep in copyright fight with news orgs
entry.summary: News organizations led by the New York Times filed a sanctions motion accusing OpenAI of concealing evidence and misrepresenting its ability to search training logs in the copyright dispute. The contested logs could show whether users used ChatGPT to bypass paywalls, making them pivotal to both sides.

entry.title: OpenAI wants its new tool to do your work for you and with you
entry.summary: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Work, an agent designed to stay with complex, multi-hour projects and turn a stated goal into finished deliverables across apps and files. It positions the tool as fixing earlier agent-mode limitations where automated tasks would stall after a few minutes.

entry.title: New York Times says OpenAI hid evidence in ChatGPT copyright trial
entry.summary: TechCrunch reports publishers accuse OpenAI of hiding tools and datasets that could detect copyrighted journalism in ChatGPT outputs, filing a new sanctions motion. It escalates the ongoing copyright lawsuit.

entry.title: OpenAI rolls out GPT-5.6 after government greenlight — and announces ‘ChatGPT Work’
entry.summary: OpenAI rolled out GPT-5.6 to the public after the Trump administration's greenlight and simultaneously unveiled ChatGPT Work, a combination of ChatGPT and Codex powered by the Sol, Terra, and Luna model suite. Altman called it the best model the company has produced.

entry.title: OpenAI launches its new family of models with GPT-5.6
entry.summary: TechCrunch covers OpenAI's public launch of the GPT-5.6 model family, promising broad improvements including in cybersecurity. The rollout follows the government-approved wider release.

entry.title: Meta says its new AI model is ready to compete on coding
entry.summary: Meta opened Muse Spark 1.1 to developers via a new Meta Model API, describing it as a step-change with advanced coding, end-to-end agentic workflows, multi-agent support, and native multimodal perception. It follows Meta's April reentry into the model race.

entry.title: OpenAI pairs its GPT-5.6 public rollout with ChatGPT Work, a new agent that handles entire workflows
entry.summary: OpenAI paired its GPT-5.6 public rollout with ChatGPT Work, an agent powered by Codex and GPT-5.6 that can independently handle complex projects across apps like Google Drive, Slack, and Salesforce. It is available on web, mobile, and desktop with access tied to subscription tier.

entry.title: Databricks makes Chinese open-source model GLM 5.2 its default coding engine after it matched Opus at lower cost
entry.summary: Databricks benchmarked coding agents on its own multi-million-line codebase and found the Chinese open-source model GLM 5.2 matched Anthropic's Opus 4.8 at lower cost, planning to adopt it as a daily coding workhorse. Its takeaway is that no single provider dominates and firms should build their own benchmarks.

entry.title: ChatGPT is now a partner for your most ambitious work
entry.summary: OpenAI's official announcement describes ChatGPT Work as an agent that takes actions across apps and files, can persist on a project for hours, and turns a goal into finished output. It is the company's flagship push into agentic productivity.

entry.title: Meta’s new AI chips will begin production in September
entry.summary: Meta's custom AI chips are set to begin production in September, built with a modular design meant to adapt as AI needs evolve. The move deepens Meta's in-house silicon strategy.

entry.title: Meta's Muse Spark 1.1 API pricing squeezes OpenAI and Anthropic as the AI price war heats up
entry.summary: Meta priced Muse Spark 1.1 API access at 4.25 dollars per million output tokens, undercutting even the newly released, cheap Grok 4.5 and far below OpenAI and Anthropic. The move sharpens the AI price war for pure-play labs burning cash.

entry.title: GPT-5.6: Frontier intelligence that scales with your ambition
entry.summary: OpenAI's official page for GPT-5.6 emphasizes more intelligence per token, stronger performance per dollar, and scalable capability for demanding work. It accompanies the model's public availability.

entry.title: OpenAI is shutting down Atlas, but its AI browser ambitions are still growing
entry.summary: OpenAI is sunsetting its Atlas AI browser less than a year after launch, moving agentic browsing into its desktop app and a Chrome extension. The move reflects a strategy to cut side projects and consolidate around productivity via ChatGPT Work.

entry.title: Anthropic, OpenAI, and SpaceX are bigger than the last 25 years of tech exits
entry.summary: TechCrunch reports that anticipated IPOs of Anthropic, OpenAI, and SpaceX could generate more value than all US VC-backed exits since 2000. It underscores the scale of value concentrating in AI-linked companies.

entry.title: Anthropic found a hidden space where Claude puzzles over concepts
entry.summary: Anthropic built an interpretability technique called the Jacobian lens that reveals a hidden internal region, dubbed J-space, in Claude Opus 4.6 containing words related to what the model is likely to say next. Researchers describe findings ranging from mundane to unnerving.

entry.title: How did the government decide OpenAI’s frontier model was safe to release?
entry.summary: The piece examines how the US government determined OpenAI's frontier model was safe enough for public release, noting the dialogue between officials and both OpenAI and Anthropic remains opaque. It probes the emerging government role in release decisions.

entry.title: GPT-5.6 Sol nearly matches Fable 5 on aggregated benchmarks at one-third the cost
entry.summary: Benchmarks show OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol scoring 59 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, one point behind Claude Fable 5, while costing about a third as much per task. Sol reportedly leads all competitors in agentic coding, intensifying pricing pressure on Anthropic.

entry.title: OpenAI finds roughly 30 percent of popular AI coding test is broken
entry.summary: OpenAI reviewed the widely used SWE-Bench Pro coding benchmark and found roughly 30 percent of its tasks are broken, withdrawing its earlier endorsement. The finding undermines confidence in a common measure of AI programming skill.

entry.title: Large Tabular Models Excel Where LLMs Fail
entry.summary: The article describes large tabular models as a new class of generative AI aimed at structured spreadsheet data, where LLMs typically fail. It argues most enterprise-critical data sits in tables that current chatbots cannot handle well.

entry.title: OpenAI’s CEO of AGI Deployment, Fidji Simo, Is Stepping Down
entry.summary: Fidji Simo, OpenAI's chief of AGI deployment, is stepping down from her full-time role after an extended medical leave and will remain a part-time adviser. The departure follows other recent senior exits at the company.

entry.title: Paris-based AI voice startup Gradium raises $100M seed, backed by Nvidia
entry.summary: Paris-based AI voice startup Gradium raised a 100-million-dollar seed round backed by Nvidia and plans a Bay Area office to compete for talent. The founders are linked to the Kyutai research lab.

entry.title: The ChatGPT browser is already dead
entry.summary: OpenAI confirmed it will sunset the ChatGPT Atlas browser with a targeted August 9 deprecation, less than a year after launch. Agentic browsing features move into the desktop superapp and a Chrome extension amid the ChatGPT Work push.

entry.title: Fidji Simo steps down from OpenAI’s no. 2 role
entry.summary: TechCrunch reports Fidji Simo is stepping down from OpenAI's number-two role after her medical leave ran longer than expected. The exit comes as OpenAI eyes a possible IPO and races Anthropic in enterprise.

entry.title: Fidji Simo steps down from leading OpenAI’s AGI work due to illness
entry.summary: The Verge reports Fidji Simo is leaving her full-time AGI-chief role at OpenAI to become a part-time adviser due to a neuroimmune condition. Her exit follows other recent senior departures at the company.

entry.title: An AI agent startup just let its agent run its $100M fundraise
entry.summary: Enterprise agent startup Lyzr says it used its own AI agent to run a 100-million-dollar fundraising round, presenting it as proof its product works. The round crosses the significant-funding threshold.

entry.title: Instagram’s AI image generator alarms privacy experts
entry.summary: Privacy advocates warned that Meta's newly released Muse Image tool lets users generate pictures of people with public Instagram profiles by default, without notifying those individuals. Users are advised to review privacy settings.

entry.title: Popular open source AI developer tool Ollama raises $65M, grows to nearly 9M users
entry.summary: Open-source local-inference tool Ollama raised 65 million dollars from Benchmark and grew to nearly 9 million users, with heavy GitHub traction. It helps developers run AI models on their own machines.

entry.title: GPT-5.6 is now the preferred model in Microsoft 365 Copilot
entry.summary: OpenAI announced GPT-5.6 is now the preferred model in Microsoft 365 Copilot, powering Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Chat, and Cowork. It positions the model for faster, higher-quality productivity work.

entry.title: Elon Musk praises Mythos/Fable, promises not to ‘cut off’ Anthropic
entry.summary: Elon Musk publicly praised Anthropic's Mythos and Fable models and pledged not to cut off Anthropic, which reportedly has around 40 billion dollars in revenue at stake in a hosting relationship. The piece questions whether Anthropic should trust Musk's infrastructure.

entry.title: Anthropic Wants You to Pay Up for Claude Fable 5
entry.summary: Anthropic will require Claude subscribers to pay usage-based fees to access its top consumer model, Claude Fable 5. The shift is framed as a signal that flat-rate AI subscriptions are giving way to metered pricing.

entry.title: GPT-5.5 Bio Bug Bounty
entry.summary: OpenAI detailed a GPT-5.5 Bio bug bounty program focused on safety, inviting scrutiny of the model's handling of biological-risk concerns. It is framed as part of the company's safety efforts.

entry.title: NHS AI blood test could reduce invasive womb cancer checks
entry.summary: Several NHS hospitals are preparing to deploy PinPoint, a machine-learning blood test that scores womb-cancer risk from about 30 markers, to reduce invasive checks. The roughly 30-pound test slots into existing referral pathways for tens of thousands of women annually.

entry.title: Google will now disclose which ads are made with AI
entry.summary: Google will now let users see whether ads on Search, Discover, and YouTube were created or edited with AI, via a new label in My Ad Center. Previously such disclosure was required only for election ads.

entry.title: Google will now tell you if an ad was made with AI
entry.summary: The Verge details Google's new My Ad Center label showing whether ads across Search, Discover, and YouTube were created or edited with AI. Ads made with Google's own tools are labeled automatically; others require manual disclosure.

entry.title: AWS GraphRAG deployment cuts drug research cycles by 87%
entry.summary: An AWS GraphRAG deployment reportedly cut pharmaceutical R&D cycles by 87 percent by unifying siloed proprietary databases into a queryable knowledge graph combined with NLP. It targets early data-gathering and screening phases that previously took months per iteration.

entry.title: Instagram users: Here’s how to stop Meta’s AI from using your photos
entry.summary: A how-to explains that Meta's Muse Image can generate AI pictures from any public Instagram account's photos when tagged, and details how users can restrict this. It centers on protecting personal images.

entry.title: Grok 4.5 is so cheap compared to Fable 5 and GPT 5.5 that benchmark gaps may not matter much
entry.summary: xAI released Grok 4.5, trained on tens of thousands of Nvidia GB300 GPUs, which trails Fable 5 and GPT-5.5 in coding benchmarks but uses roughly 4.2 times fewer tokens than Opus 4.8. At 2 dollars per million input tokens it is far cheaper than rivals, with EU availability expected mid-July.

entry.title: Meta enters the crowded AI coding battle with Muse Spark 1.1
entry.summary: Meta released Muse Spark 1.1, positioning it for large agentic coding workloads, complex bug fixing, and large-scale code migrations. The pitch targets enterprises increasingly outsourcing automation to AI providers.

entry.title: Grok 4.5 Is SpaceXAI’s First Real Entry Into the Enterprise
entry.summary: The piece frames Grok 4.5 as SpaceXAI's first real enterprise entry, its first model release since SpaceX's June IPO, aimed at competing with frontier providers particularly on coding. It positions the release as a push into the enterprise market.

entry.title: [AINews] SpaceXAI launches Grok 4.5, first Opus-class model post Cursor acquisition
entry.summary: A newsletter recap covers SpaceXAI's Grok 4.5 launch, its first Opus-class model following a Cursor acquisition, noting it is a heavier weight class than the Composer series and performs comparably to Opus and GPT workhorses. It also flags that SWE-Bench Pro appears saturated or flawed ahead of GPT-5.6's launch.

entry.title: The $28 Million Mistake That Inspired Estonia’s AI ‘Fuckup Finder’
entry.summary: Estonia built an AI tool to catch legal drafting errors before laws take effect, prompted by a single wording mistake that cost the government tens of millions. The effort is part of a broader push to automate state functions.

entry.title: Can AI answer the $3 trillion question?
entry.summary: The article revisits the AI return-on-investment debate, framing it around a roughly 3-trillion-dollar question of whether massive capex will pay off. It notes the stakes and consequences have grown.

entry.title: Anthropic’s new Claude feature is quietly selling you on AI
entry.summary: Anthropic's new Claude Reflect dashboard visualizes users' AI usage patterns while, TechCrunch argues, subtly reinforcing dependence on the chatbot. It mirrors year-in-review style features from consumer apps.

entry.title: Say hello to Claude Wrapped
entry.summary: Anthropic launched Claude Reflect, a Wrapped-style dashboard summarizing a user's key topics, delegated tasks, and usage patterns over selectable time ranges. It is pitched as helping users see and shape their AI habits.

entry.title: Character.AI wants a piece of the microdrama pie
entry.summary: Character.AI debuted c.ai Series, short animated episodic videos made almost entirely with generative AI that viewers can watch and interact with. It targets the fast-growing microdrama market.

entry.title: Character.AI enters the microdrama arena with its own productions, but there’s a twist
entry.summary: Character.AI is entering short-form microdramas with its own productions, letting viewers chat with and roleplay alongside the shows' characters. The format leans on its core conversational-character product.

entry.title: IBM Extends Bob AI Platform With Array of New Features
entry.summary: IBM expanded its Bob AI platform with an array of new features, described as a significant enlargement of the platform's capabilities. Details in the summary are sparse.

entry.title: FL Studio 2026 turns its AI chatbot into your assistant engineer
entry.summary: FL Studio 2026 upgraded its Gopher assistant from an instruction-lookup chatbot into one that can execute music-production actions, such as laying down beats and applying effects. It still cannot draw automation or insert notes directly.

entry.title: The fight against AI data centers is important – but it’s just a starting point | Bruce Schneier and Nathan E Sanders

author.name: Bruce Schneier and Nathan E Sanders

entry.summary: An opinion piece argues that opposition to AI data centers, while legitimate, distracts from the larger risk of AI firms concentrating wealth, power, and political influence. The authors urge broader scrutiny beyond local infrastructure fights.

entry.title: Enhancing enterprise inference on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod with data capture, Hugging Face, NVMe, and Route 53 integration
entry.summary: AWS detailed new SageMaker HyperPod features for enterprise inference, including multi-point data capture, direct deployment from community model hubs, NVMe, and Route 53 integration. The updates target observability, flexibility, and scale for production models.

entry.title: MCP tool design: Practical approaches and tradeoffs
entry.summary: An AWS engineering post argues that most Model Context Protocol tool failures stem from poor tool design rather than the protocol, and offers context-engineering fixes for issues like definition bloat and wrong parameters. It targets teams building agentic systems.

entry.title: AI tool scours the web for job openings, preps your resume and cover letter
entry.summary: A developer built Autopilot-Jobhunt, a tool that scans the web overnight for job openings matching a user's profile, scores and ranks them, and can draft tailored resumes and cover letters. It notifies users via Telegram with results.
